title.narrative: WFP Resilience Programme 2026 - Green Skills Development

description.narrative: Cox’s Bazar, Bangladesh, has become the epicentre of a prolonged humanitarian crisis, hosting over 900,000 Forcibly Displaced Myanmar Nationals (FDMNs) alongside vulnerable host communities. This crisis has led to significant socio-economic and environmental challenges, including heightened pressures on local resources, increased vulnerability to natural disasters, and limited livelihood opportunities. Humanitarian organizations are providing crucial support; however, funding shortfalls have led to reductions in food assistance, leaving many refugees with as little as $8 a month for food (WFP, 2023). Addressing these issues requires a multifaceted approach that strengthens resilience, enhances food security, and builds sustainable livelihoods. The World Food Programme (WFP) has been actively engaged in mitigating these challenges through its Cox’s Bazar Resilience Programme, focusing on building community resilience through natural resource management, youth engagement, and market linkage promotion. This programme is critical in aligning humanitarian efforts with long-term development goals to support both Rohingya refugees and host communities. In line with WFP’s objectives, Cordaid’s proposal aims to contribute to green skills development within refugee camps through activities such as homestead gardening, aquaculture, mushroom cultivation, and solid waste management. These activities will not only supplement food security but also promote ecofriendly practices that contribute to environmental restoration. The initiative will engage youth and other vulnerable groups in developing skills that align with sustainable practices, thereby building resilience against environmental and socio-economic shocks. The environmental degradation in Cox’s Bazar, exacerbated by the demands for firewood and agricultural space, has significantly impacted forest resources, increasing the risks of landslides and other disasters. Green skills development within camps offers a pathway to reduce environmental impact while fostering self-reliance among the refugee population. Moreover, with Cox’s Bazar designated as an 'ecologically critical area,' sustainable practices in food production and waste management are essential to safeguarding the region's natural resources. Cordaid’s extensive experience in resilience programming, coupled with a focus on sustainable livelihoods, can contribute significantly to achieving the goals. By integrating climate-smart agricultural techniques and waste reduction practices, Cordaid’s approach aligns with WFP’s commitment to enhancing food systems and building resilience against shocks. This project will support Cox’s Bazar’s most vulnerable communities, empowering them with green skills that promote self-reliance and sustainability in the face of ongoing challenges. On that note, in alignment with the organization's track record and expertise, Cordaid in Bangladesh would like to offer support to WFP Bangladesh in addressing challenges around green skills, capacity strengthening and building the resilience of the local community, market linkage and anticipatory action activities.

• Improve Household Food Security through Climate-Smart Agricultural Practices such as homestead gardening, aquaculture, and mushroom production systems that enhance local food security by enabling 21,100 (20,000 homestead gardening, 1,000 aquaculturess, and 100 mushroom) participants to grow climate-resilient crops and produce fresh fish and mushrooms. • Develop green skills training programs focused on composting and plastic waste upcycling (1200 participants) that will equip participants with marketable skills and promote eco-friendly economic activities within the camps and host communities. • Equip participants with climate-adaptive techniques such as raised-bed gardening and pond-dyke vegetable cultivation to build resilience against climate risks/shocks. Training on sustainable aquaculture and other adaptive agricultural methods will help communities better withstand and recover from natural disasters, such as floods and landslides, common to Cox’s Bazar reducing their overall vulnerability. • improve self-esteem and preventing Rohingya youths from engaging in anti-social activities and improving community resilience.
